Rents in Alfama and Graça have doubled since 2016, and long-time residents describe streets they no longer recognise, with laundry lines replaced by lockboxes and grocers by shops selling tinned fish to visitors. (section 1)
The city council's response has been a patchwork of licence freezes and tax changes that critics say arrived years late, and that owners' groups have challenged in court at every step. (section 1)
Tourism now accounts for a fifth of the city's economy, a figure that makes any retreat politically costly for a mayor who was elected on a promise to bring the numbers down. (section 1)
